name: smarthire-ai
description: Smart Hire AI — Electron desktop app and its Next.js licensing backend
_comment_rename: RENAME 2026-09-06: apps/site -> apps/marketing and apps/web -> apps/dashboard, and every workspace name is now scoped @smarthire/*. "site" and "web" were one letter of meaning apart and the pair had to be memorised; the new names say which surface they are. apps/admin and apps/desktop kept their names because those were already unambiguous. WHAT DID NOT MOVE WITH IT: (1) the Vercel projects are still NAMED web, site and admin — deliberately, because renaming the web project breaks every packaged desktop build — but the Build Command and the Ignored Build Step inside the web and site projects still say build:web / build:site and apps/web / apps/site, and only the Vercel dashboard can fix them. The stale build command fails loudly; the stale Ignored Build Step fails SILENTLY, because a path matching nothing diffs clean, git diff --quiet exits 0, and Vercel reads 0 as skip — see "Deploying" in the README. (2) The one COMMENT ON string that is real applied DDL (supabase/migrations/20260830020000_resume_files.sql) keeps apps/web, because that is the text the live database already stores; the inert -- comments in those migrations were updated.
_comment_workspaces: SPLIT 2026-09-01: packages/* are listed FIRST so npm links them before the apps that depend on them. @smarthire/pricing has no dependencies and no peer dependencies at all — that is what keeps apps/desktop (React 18, Tailwind 3, pinned deliberately; see the version note in the README) able to consume it one day without npm resolving a second React into the tree. ADMIN SPLIT 2026-09-01: apps/* is NOT globbed, so apps/admin had to be added by hand here — without this entry npm links nothing into apps/admin/node_modules, `npm run dev:admin` does not exist, and the failure looks like a broken script rather than a missing workspace.
_comment_dev: SPLIT 2026-09-01: `dev` keeps meaning "everything", which is now FOUR processes. `dev:front` is the loop most work actually needs, and it deliberately does NOT include admin: three Next servers plus Electron under the 512MB cap is heavy, and most work touches marketing and dashboard. Reach for `dev:console` when the work is on admin — it runs the app beside it, which is what you want, because the two share a Supabase project and the cookie-isolation check (sign in at 3000, open 3003, it must still ask you to sign in) needs both. The ports are not interchangeable: apps/desktop/.env points WEB_URL at 127.0.0.1:3000, so if another app could take that port the desktop would silently talk to it.

scripts.dev: concurrently -n marketing,dashboard,admin,desktop -c green,cyan,yellow,magenta "npm run dev:marketing" "npm run dev:dashboard" "npm run dev:admin" "npm run dev:desktop"
scripts.dev:front: concurrently -n marketing,dashboard -c green,cyan "npm run dev:marketing" "npm run dev:dashboard"
scripts.dev:console: concurrently -n dashboard,admin -c cyan,yellow "npm run dev:dashboard" "npm run dev:admin"
